title: Backyard homes
summary: Allow an extra small home on qualifying residential lots.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Allow one small additional home on every residential lot, with a standard approval path and no new infrastructure funding.

amendment.text: Allow one small additional home on qualifying residential lots. Publish infrastructure capacity checks, offer low-interest construction loans, and review rents and displacement after two years.
amendment.summary: Add capacity checks, construction loans and a two-year displacement review; administration and public costs increase.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: extra homes ease some supply pressure, while utility capacity and construction finance constrain delivery. These are authored model inputs.

title: Third places for everyone
summary: Open neighborhood places to meet, learn and spend time without buying anything.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Build a new staffed public gathering space in every neighborhood, open every day and free to enter.

amendment.text: Run a one-year third-place pilot in existing libraries and community buildings, with accessible evening hours and an independently reviewed expansion budget.
amendment.summary: Reuse existing buildings and cap the pilot budget; coverage and opening hours are smaller than the original promise.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: reusing buildings lowers modeled cost, while staffing and accessible travel remain constraints. No real-world impact estimate is asserted.

title: Private civic journal
summary: Let residents turn private notes into proposals they choose to share.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Create a public civic journal service. Automatically analyze every submitted note and store the full note indefinitely to help generate proposed laws.

amendment.text: Create an opt-in civic journal. Keep notes private by default, process only specifically shared excerpts, permit deletion and export, and publish security review findings before launch.
amendment.summary: Add explicit sharing consent, deletion, export and security review; usefulness, speed and operating costs face tradeoffs.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: centralized indefinite retention increases modeled privacy risk; adding controls makes implementation slower. This is a designed stress case.

title: Autonomous shuttle pilot
summary: Try a small driverless shuttle service on a limited route.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Deploy autonomous public shuttles across the city immediately, recording all rides to improve service and replacing existing routes.

amendment.text: Run a six-month autonomous shuttle pilot on one accessible route, with a safety operator, published stop criteria, short data retention, and existing transit routes retained.
amendment.summary: Limit the route, retain existing transit and add safety and data protections; coverage stays narrow and the pilot costs more per rider.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: reliability, accessibility and total operating cost are uncertain; no claim of real-world safety or savings is made.

title: Rain-ready neighborhoods
summary: Upgrade drainage and shaded public space in flood-exposed neighborhoods.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Fund drainage upgrades and rain gardens citywide through a uniform household fee, beginning with projects that are easiest to build.

amendment.text: Fund drainage upgrades and rain gardens first in high-exposure neighborhoods. Exempt low-income households from the fee and publish project delivery and maintenance costs.
amendment.summary: Prioritize exposure and exempt low-income households; larger public subsidy and more complex delivery reduce some budget gains.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: flood exposure and upkeep differ by neighborhood; the scenario assigns unequal impacts without claiming a measured forecast.

title: Open contracts ledger
summary: Make spending decisions and contract changes easier to inspect.
provenance: Invented Helios-inspired proposal for interface testing; not a real bill introduced today.

initial.text: Publish every public contract and supplier document immediately in a searchable public ledger, including all contact and bank details.

amendment.text: Publish public contracts, awards and amendments in a searchable ledger. Redact personal and bank details, show reasons for redactions, and allow independent review of withheld records.
amendment.summary: Redact sensitive details and add review; moderation costs and slower publication trade off against privacy.

evidence.summary: Scenario assumption: detailed publication helps inspection but unredacted records expose sensitive data. Model weights express the tradeoff, not measured savings.
